title: "Solutions: Cleaning and tidying medical data"

::: {.callout-note}
These are the solutions to the
[Cleaning and tidying](../lecture-02/02-clean-and-tidy.qmd) exercises.
Try each exercise yourself before you look.
:::

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(medicaldata)
```

## Exercise 1: Gum health over the trial's visits

```{r}
gums <- opt |>
  select(PID, Group, BL.GE, BL.PD.avg, V3.GE, V3.PD.avg, V5.GE, V5.PD.avg)

gums_tidy <- gums |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(PID, Group),
    names_to = c("visit", "measure"),
    names_pattern = "(BL|V3|V5)\\.(.*)",
    values_to = "value",
    values_drop_na = TRUE
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = measure, values_from = value)
gums_tidy
```

```{r}
gums_summary <- gums_tidy |>
  group_by(Group, visit) |>
  summarize(
    avg_pd = mean(PD.avg, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_ge = mean(GE, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
gums_summary
```

**(3)** The treatment group's gums got better.
Its mean pocket depth fell from 2.90 mm at baseline to 2.45 mm at visit 5,
and its gingival index fell from 1.45 to 1.15,
while the control group stayed about the same.
[Linear regression](../lecture-02/04-linear-regression.qmd) asks
whether the treatment also changed birth weight.

```{r}
ggplot(gums_summary, aes(x = visit, y = avg_pd, colour = Group, group = Group)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Visit", y = "Mean pocket depth (mm)", colour = "Group")
```

## Exercise 2: Coded variables

```{r}
blood <- blood_storage |>
  mutate(
    recurrence = factor(Recurrence, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("no", "yes")),
    rbc_age_group = factor(RBC.Age.Group, levels = 1:3,
                           labels = c("younger", "middle", "older"))
  )

blood |>
  count(rbc_age_group, recurrence)
```
